sentences.text: Colymboides represents the earliest known unambiguous fossils of the order Gaviiformes, the group containing loons. These birds belong to the family Gaviidae, which includes modern loons.
The genus contains three species of early loons usually placed in the subfamily Colymboidinae, separate from the subfamily Gaviinae that holds modern-type loons.
The genus Colymboides was first described by Milne-Edwards in 1867. Three species are known: C. minutus described in 1867, C. anglicus in 1891, and C. metzleri in 2004.
The genus Colymboides has the synonym Gavioides.

These animals lived from the Rupelian to the Langhian stages, approximately 33.9 to 13.82 million years ago. Their fossils were found in rocks located between the Atlantic Ocean and the former Turgai Sea.
Researchers debate whether Colymboides belongs in the family Gaviidae or in a now-extinct family of primitive gaviiforms due to its distinct features.
